tasks.title: Nmap MSRPC Scripts
tasks.description: 135 is the DCE/RPC endpoint mapper — it doesn't do much itself, but tells you which RPC-registered services are actually available and on what dynamic port.

tasks.title: Enumerate Registered RPC Interfaces
tasks.description: Full list of every RPC interface the host exposes (often reveals which services are running even when their normal ports look closed/filtered from the outside).

tasks.title: What Actually Uses This Port
tasks.description: 135 rarely matters in isolation — it's the entry point for several techniques documented in more detail elsewhere. wmiexec/dcomexec (Impacket) use it for command execution over WMI/DCOM, and coercion attacks (PetitPotam, PrinterBug) use it to trigger the target's own machine account to authenticate back to you via MS-EFSRPC/MS-RPRN. See the SMB (445) methodology and the Active Directory Post-Exploitation section for the full attack chains.
